key_insight: BioEmu2 unifies biomolecular structure prediction, equilibrium sampling and time evolution in a generative model that samples orders of magnitude faster than molecular dynamics.
engineering_relevance: It could accelerate computational studies of multi-component biomolecular systems, including binding, conformational changes and rare-state free energies.
method: Trains on experimental structures, synthetic structures and extensive molecular dynamics data.
Generates atomically resolved systems containing proteins, nucleic acids, modified residues, ligands and ions.
Supports contact conditioning, bias-potential steering, enhanced sampling and context-parallel prediction of megadalton complexes.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports structure accuracy comparable to leading open-weight folding models and free-energy errors near 1 kcal/mol against molecular dynamics references across tested proteins and complexes.
watch_item: Accuracy of equilibrium distributions and predicted kinetics on systems outside the tested set requires validation before replacing molecular dynamics.
paper_title: BioEmu2: Scalable Emulation of Biomolecular Dynamics
